title: Boiled Potato, fresh, peel eaten, with margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Boiled potato is a dish made from fresh potatoes cooked in salted water until tender, with the skin left on and eaten. Margarine is often added for a mild, buttery flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato is the fourth most produced food crop worldwide after cereals, rice, and wheat.
Eating the skin retains most of the fiber and nutrients, especially vitamin C and potassium.
Margarine is used instead of butter because it contains less saturated fat and is more stable at high temperatures.
Boiled potatoes serve as a base for many dishes: salads, mash, casseroles, and side dishes.
Large potatoes take longer to cook, so they are often cut into uniform pieces for even boiling.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide slowly digestible carbs that help maintain steady energy levels.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium supports fluid balance, heart function, and muscle activity.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C in the skin boosts immunity and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: The peel is high in fiber, which aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Boiled potatoes themselves contain almost no fat; adding margarine lets you control the amount.

items.title: Margarine allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to vegetable oils or additives used in margarine.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salt is commonly added during boiling; excess sodium can raise blood pressure.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Potatoes have a high GI, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: Prolonged heating in water can produce small amounts of acrylamide, a potential carcinogen.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve boiled potatoes warm, drizzled with melted margarine and seasoned with fresh herbs, salt, or spices. The skin can be eaten together with the flesh, adding texture and nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool boiled potatoes to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat in the microwave or on the stove, adding fresh margarine before serving.
